To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of acquiring a 3D-HNCA and a 3D-COCA spectrum in a single NMR experiment by incorporating polarization sharing, dual receiver and parallel detection concepts.

the 3D- HACACO spectrum is a useful addition to the set of backbone and side chain correlated 3D spectra, and the parallel acquisition of 3- D-HACACO and 3D- HA(CA)NH spectra is a useful strategy to obtain the maximum amount of information in a single experiment.
a new 3D pulse sequence has been developed that allows parallel acquisition of 3-dimensional 13C detected HACACO and HCA(CO)NH spectra of proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, development and application of a novel 5D NMR pulse sequence to acquire 3D-H(A/C)A(CA)N(H) and 3D-(HA)CACO spectra of proteins.
development of a novel 3D-HNCOCA experiment, which is capable of recording simultaneously 3D-HCA(CO)NH and 2D-HN(CO)CA spectra of proteins.
the design and implementation of a 3D experiment with 5 time increments for simultaneous acquisition of 3H–13C–1H triple resonance spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D-NCA(CO)NH experiment, which is a combination of the 3D-CA(CO) and 3D-N(CA)NH, is the most efficient experiment to obtain sequential backbone assignment of proteins.
3D-HCA(CO)NH and 13C detected 3D-HNCA are the most useful for sequential assignment, whereas 3D-HCCH-TOCSY, 3D-HCACO and 3D-COCA are most useful for side chain assignment.
the 3D-NCA(CO)NH and 13C-detected 3D-HCA(CO)CO are complementary to each other and the 3D-CA(CA)CO and 13C detected 3D-CACACO are complimentary to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed 5D experiment provides 2 independent experiments (3D-HA/CANH and 3D-CACACO) with 3D-HCA(CO)NH and 2D-1Hα/1Hβ/1Hγ as by-products, all recorded within 1 experiment.
the 3D-ACACO spectrum provides backbone information of all the residues, while the 3D-A(CA)NH spectrum provides backbone and side-chain information for the residues having HN and 1Hα.

the 3D-CA(CO)HN and 3D-ACACO spectra are complementary to each other and together they provide a complete coverage of backbone correlations for all amino acids, except for prolines, in a single NMR experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual receiver concept can be used to acquire 3D experiments with multiple independent delays, and that such an approach may be useful for other applications as well.
a single 3D experiment can provide a large amount of information on a protein, and the information can be extracted in a single step, without any need to record and analyze multiple spectra.
a large number of 3D experiments can be acquired in one go using a 5D pulse sequence, thus reducing the overall experimental time by 20-fold.
